evidence: Hypothesis REFUTED on its symlink clause. Built evasion_matrix.py, which runs the live guard workstreams/po03/tools/check_path_scope.py and the hardened guard side by side over 37 cases (28 judged by name, 9 through real git diff in throwaway repositories) and prints what each guard really did against what the allowlist requires. Measured: cases=37 legacy_unsatisfied=10 hardened_unsatisfied=0, exit 0, PO03_MATRIX_PASS, captured verbatim in evidence/evasion-matrix.txt. The live guard DOES resist traversal (.. , ../x, workstreams/po03/../state/x, ./ and // spellings), unicode confusables (Cyrillic o, fullwidth w) and case variation (WORKSTREAMS/PO03/x, .github/workflows/PO03-a.yml) - recorded as REFUSES rather than invented as holes. It does NOT resist symlinks: an in-allowlist name added as mode 120000 pointing at ../../state exits 0 with PO03_PATH_SCOPE_PASS. Five real escapes were reproduced end to end: rename of state/PROTECTED.json into the allowlist (git diff --name-only shows only the post-image, so a deletion outside the allowlist is invisible, while a plain git rm of the same file IS caught), relative escaping symlink, absolute symlink target, type change from regular file to escaping symlink, and a mode 160000 gitlink inside the allowlist. A sixth divergence: .github/workflows/po03-a/b.yml is admitted by the guard's prefix-plus-suffix test although the commissioned glob .github/workflows/po03-*.yml does not cross a directory boundary. Shipped hardened_path_scope.py, which judges both images of a rename from git diff --raw -z --no-abbrev -M, resolves and judges symlink targets, refuses gitlinks and unexpected modes, and matches the workflow allowlist as a segment-aware glob. Ran python3 -I -m unittest discover over the unit subtree: 43 tests, OK, exit 0, captured in evidence/test-run.txt, including a test asserting the legacy guard admits the rename and the symlink so the refutation itself is a regression guard, and tests confirming legitimate in-allowlist changes and an in-allowlist symlink are still admitted.
falsifiable_hypothesis: The path-scope guard resists traversal, symlink, unicode and case-variation evasion.
limitations: The hardened guard lives in this unit's subtree and does not replace workstreams/po03/tools/check_path_scope.py, which this producer must not modify; until a controller installs it the five escapes remain open in the live gate.

Four of the ten legacy gaps are deliberate narrowings rather than escapes: trailing-dot and trailing-space components and non-ASCII or bidi names are inside the allowlist and are refused on portability and review-integrity grounds, not because they leave scope. Refusing all non-ASCII paths is policy, not necessity, and would need replacing with an NFC or script-mixing rule if PO-03 ever needs a non-ASCII artifact name.

The NUL evasion class cannot be delivered through either real channel: argv rejects an embedded NUL with ValueError before any guard runs, and git diff -z uses NUL as its field separator while git forbids NUL in path names. That row is judged in process and the matrix records its channel as such rather than implying an argv test occurred.
Symlink judgement requires reading the blob body, so a change set handed to the guard without repository access is refused as SYMLINK_UNVERIFIABLE; fail-closed, but not usable in a name-only context.
The guard judges a change set between two commits and says nothing about which base a workflow chooses, so a gate computing the wrong base can still be fed a change set that hides a mutation.
